title: Employment Situation (Sep 2027 data) — 08:30 ET, a second-Friday release that leaves the October expiry five sessions instead of ten
source: EST: derived from BLS's own published scheduling rule — release on the third Friday following the end of the reference week (the Sun-Sat week containing the 12th). THE RULE WAS RE-IMPLEMENTED AND RE-VALIDATED FROM SCRATCH BY THIS EVENT'S OWN never-assessed RESEARCH (2026-09-09) rather than inherited from the proposal: 7 for 7 against the four confirmed jobs-* entries on this calendar (2026-09-04, 2026-10-02, 2026-11-06, 2026-12-04) and the three historical Sunday-July-4 releases (2004-07-02, 2010-07-02, 2021-07-02). September 2027's 12th is a SUNDAY, so the reference week is Sun 2027-09-12 to Sat 2027-09-18 and the third Friday after 09-18 is 2027-10-08 — a SECOND-Friday release rather than the usual first-Friday one. 2027-10-08 is an ordinary NYSE trading day; the rule's one documented failure mode is a holiday landing on its own Friday, and the nearest holiday is Columbus Day on Mon 2027-10-11, which FOLLOWS the print and never displaces it. The prefix is EST: and not BLS: because bls.gov returned HTTP 403 to a browser user-agent on all four schedule routes re-tried on 2026-09-09 (/schedule/news_release/2027_sched.htm, /schedule/news_release/empsit.htm, /schedule/home.htm, /bls/news-release/empsit.htm) and fred.stlouisfed.org/release/dates?rid=50 returned HTTP 404 — all five recorded in this event's probe-ref.blocked. A derived date is not a published one
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN BY THIS EVENT'S OWN never-assessed RESEARCH (2026-09-09), superseding proposals/jobs-2027-10-08.from-jobs-2027-09-03.json, which stays where it is and is now shadowed. WHAT THIS SESSION ESTABLISHED THAT THE PROPOSAL DID NOT. (1) THE PROPOSAL'S ANALOGUE LIST IS INCOMPLETE — 1999 IS MISSING. It named 1993, 2004, 2010 and 2021 as the Sunday-September-12th years resolving to an October 8 release; the rule run over 1993-2027 emits 1999-10-08 as well, so the analogue set is FIVE (1993, 1999, 2004, 2010, 2021) not four. Corrected here rather than carried. (2) THE 'LOOKS WRONG' FRAMING IS RIGHT BUT THE RARITY IS OVERSTATED. A second-Friday release is 34 of 419 releases 1993-2027 (8.1%), not an oddity — and it is structurally confined to five release-months (Mar 13, then May/Jul/Oct/Dec 5 each; never Jan/Feb/Apr/Jun/Aug/Sep/Nov). A 35-day inter-print gap, which the proposal implied was the unusual part, is 146 of 419 (35%) and is thoroughly ordinary. Do not 'correct' the date to 2027-10-01. (3) THE SEASONAL HOLE THE PROPOSAL FLAGGED IS NOW FILLED, AND OCTOBER IS A THIRD DISTINCT PROFILE. Payroll-day amplification (the month's payroll-session median |move| over that same month's non-payroll median, which divides the month out), Yahoo split/dividend-adjusted bars 1993-2026: October is EQUITY-side, ranks QQQ 4/12 (1.55x), ^VIX 5/12 (1.37x), SPY 6/12 (1.34x) — and RATES-side dead last, IEF 12/12 (1.01x: the payroll session moves IEF no more than an ordinary October session), AGG 12/12 (1.26x), LQD 11/12 (1.19x), TLT 8/12 (1.40x). That is the mirror of jobs-2027-08-06's August (TLT/IEF/AGG ranks 1/1/1) and different again from jobs-2027-09-03's September (quiet everywhere, SPY 11/12, QQQ 12/12). Three consecutive payrolls, three profiles; the amplification instruction is month-keyed and rotates which asset class it favours. (4) THE ONE STRUCTURAL FACT THAT SURVIVES EVERY CONTROL IS ARITHMETIC, NOT BEHAVIOURAL. A second-Friday payroll leaves exactly 5 trading sessions to the same-month opex against 10 for a first-Friday one (n=33 vs 371, medians exact) — opex-2027-10-15 is at D+7. The print's share of that window's realised variance therefore roughly quadruples in SPY (21.5% vs 5.7%, 3.76x, P=0.0007, leave-one-out 33/33, both eras) — but per-session realised vol inside the window is UNCHANGED (SPY 0.80x P=0.13, every other instrument P>=0.15) and the print's own |move| is unchanged (all P>=0.13), and matching the window length to 5 sessions on both sides collapses the share effect to 1.96x P=0.085, or 1.17x P=0.36 excluding the March-heavy cases. The calendar halves the runway; the tape does not change. (5) THE SIBLING'S LONG-WEEKEND MECHANIC DOES NOT REPLICATE ON THE ASYMMETRIC CLOSURE AT D+3. sifma-bond-holiday-close-2027-10-11 shuts the cash bond market while NYSE trades. Over the 19 October payrolls whose next session is Columbus Day, not one duration leg is amplified: TLT D+1 0.71x, D+2 0.40x; IEF 1.06x / 0.75x; LQD 0.46x / 0.80x; AGG 1.21x / 0.80x — 0 of 8 above 1.0x in the direction jobs-2027-09-03 measured 5-of-5 significant for a full closure. What does reproduce is the liquidity warning that ledger already owns: TLT-minus-SPY relative volume on the closed Monday is -0.346 against 0.001 after an ordinary payroll (P=0.0027, n=13). (6) COORDINATES: fomc-minutes-2027-10-06 at D-2, sifma-bond-holiday-close-2027-10-11 at D+3, eia-steo-2027-10-13 at D+5, opex-2027-10-15 at D+7, fomc-blackout-start-2027-10-16 at D+8, vix-expiration-2027-10-20 at D+12, fomc-2027-10-26 at D+18. From federalreserve.gov's own 2027 calendar re-fetched this session (HTTP 200, page-stated 'Last Update: August 19, 2026'), this is the FIRST payroll after the September 14-15* SEP meeting and the ONLY one the October 26-27 meeting sees — the next release by the same rule is 2027-11-05, proposed in this PR. HONEST LIMITS. STATUS IS ESTIMATE AND MUST STAY THERE until bls.gov's 2027 schedule is actually retrieved; promotion trigger is any successful fetch of it naming this date, which flips the prefix to BLS: and the status to confirmed. impact high and symbols [] match every other jobs-* entry. Estimates widen caution and license no entry.
